This opportunity is intended to be undertaken as an **unpaid, university\-approved vocational or Work Integrated Learning (WIL) placement**, subject to approval by the student’s university.

It is designed for current engineering students who would like to gain supervised practical experience across solar, battery storage and smart energy projects while completing their university studies.

**Eligible Students**

Applicants must be currently studying:

* Electrical Engineering
* Renewable Energy Engineering
* Energy Engineering
* Power Systems
* Mechatronic Engineering
* A related engineering discipline

**About Us**

**Aussie Hybrid Solar** is the customer\-facing solar and battery installation service brand operated by **JT Solar Technology Pty Ltd**, a Sydney\-based renewable energy technology company established in 2009\.

JT Solar Technology has established a **Joint Battery Testing Laboratory with UNSW**, supporting applied research into battery performance, safety, reliability and compatibility.

We also participate in government\-supported clean energy initiatives, including projects delivered through the **Trailblazer for Recycling and Clean Energy (TRaCE) program**.

**What You May Work On**

During the placement, students may:

* Review solar and battery project documentation
* Review technical data sheets, product manuals and equipment specifications
* Assist with supervised analysis of solar generation, energy usage and battery performance data
* Support technical records, data summaries and draft reports
* Review testing, installation and commissioning documentation
* Research renewable energy technologies and technical questions
* Compare equipment specifications and system information
* Observe how engineering and project teams coordinate real renewable energy projects

All engineering\-related activities will be completed under appropriate supervision.

Students will **not undertake licensed electrical work, live electrical work or unsupervised high\-risk activities**.

**What You Will Gain**

* Practical exposure to **real solar, battery and smart energy projects**
* Experience with technical documentation and project processes
* Insight into renewable energy system design, testing and commissioning
* Exposure to equipment specifications and system performance data
* Development of technical research and problem\-solving skills
* Professional guidance and feedback from experienced team members

**Applicants must:**

* Be currently enrolled at an Australian university
* Have an interest in solar, battery storage and smart energy systems
* Be organised, responsible and willing to learn
* Be available to attend the placement in person

Experience with **AutoCAD, electrical design software, Microsoft Excel, data analysis, technical report writing or equipment data sheets** would be beneficial but is not essential.

**Placement Arrangement**

* **Location:** Sydney, NSW — In person
* **Duration:** Approximately 1–3 months, depending on university requirements
* The attendance schedule will be agreed based on approved placement requirements and student availability.

Any future paid casual or part\-time opportunities would be recruited separately and are **not guaranteed as part of this placement**.

**How to Apply**

Please send your **resume and a short introduction** to:

**info@aussiehybridsolar.com.au**

Please include:

* Your university, degree and current year of study
* Your required placement days or hours
* Your proposed placement dates and availability

The Ramsay Pharmacy Internship Program is designed to equip interns with the foundational knowledge, skills and confidence required to become capable and skilled pharmacists.

* Opportunities to attend industry conferences and explore career pathways across hospital, community, operations and leadership
* Attractive remuneration, employee benefits and work flexibility to support work\-life balance

Gowrie NSW is a proud not\-for\-profit early and middle childhood learning organisation established with a vision to see children thrive and amplify their contributions to the world. We are a not\-for\-profit OSHC service that places high value in creating a safe, play\-based environment for children to thrive. Our passionate team of educators strive to create a nurturing learning environment for the children in our care whilst ensuring they also have fun. Have a passion for working with children

To apply, please upload your most recent resume.

At Gowrie NSW, we believe in providing a safe, secure and nurturing environment for all children in our care. All potential employees must be willing to undergo a thorough background check and adhere to our policies and procedures. Join our team at Gowrie NSW and help us ensure the safety of children.

**Year 12 Project Coordinator**

**Are you seeking an inspiring teaching role in a supportive and vibrant environment?**


Parkerville Steiner College, located in the Perth Hills Western Australia, invites applications for a Class 12 Project Coordinator and HASS teacher. You will guide our senior students as they cross the threshold into adulthood with independence, responsibility, and purpose.


*“Since joining Parkerville Steiner College, I have felt re\-energised as an educator. I am more attuned to the rhythm and flow of lessons, and I experience a renewed joy in planning learning sequences that allow deeper understanding to unfold.”*


*“The space we are given as teachers to explore Main Lesson topics in depth is inspiring. I wish every young person had the opportunity to learn this way.”*

  



**Why Join Us?**


At Parkerville Steiner College, you’ll find a unique opportunity to teach in an environment that prioritises meaningful relationships over technology, where student behaviour is generally positive and manageable, allowing teachers to spend the great majority of their time doing what they came into the profession to do – teaching, engaging and inspiring young people.

  



**You’ll enjoy:**


* **A Balanced Workload:** No after\-school sports commitments or early\-morning meetings.
* **Professional Growth Opportunities:** Inspiring professional development with a balance of academic, artistic, and practical elements.
* **Minimal Behaviour Management:** Teach motivated students in small, engaging classes that allow you to focus on what you love – teaching.
* **Mentoring and support:** If you are new to Steiner Education, your timetable will include Pedagogical Studies, and access to a mentor.
* **Ample DOTT Time:** Ample time for non\-instruction tasks to support your work in the classroom
* **Serene Natural Setting:** Drive away from the traffic into the beautiful Perth Hills, just 20 minutes from Midland.
* **Practical Classroom Support:** A dedicated Science Technician to assist with lesson preparation, and an EA for Main Lessons.
* **Financial Benefits:**
	+ Competitive salaries similar to DOE pay rates.
	+ Salary packaging options to boost your take\-home pay.
	+ Relocation assistance available for quality interstate candidates.
* **Employee Wellbeing:** Access our Employee Assistance Program for additional support.

  

**The Role**


This role offers a rare opportunity to combine teaching HASS, educational leadership and active individual mentoring of students in their final year.

  



**Class 12 Projects:**

In Term 1 2027, you will take responsibility for the 18 or so Year 12 students and actively guide and support them through their Year 12 Independent Projects.


The projects are a unique feature of Steiner Education which involves each student researching a question or theme and:


* Writing a formal essay on their project topic, fully referenced.
* Creating and completing a practical initiative linked to their project topic – something “in the world”.
* Giving a formal 30\-minute presentation to the school community on their Project – think TED talk.
* Keeping a detailed journal of their Project experience.

This Independent Project is directly linked to whether a student graduates from a Steiner school and is the culmination of their school experience from childhood to becoming an adult. It’s often remarked that it is a wonderful privilege to do this type of work with motivated and creative young people. You will be well supported, and we are fortunate to have relatively minimal behaviour issues in our school. So, you can be a teacher!

  



**Humanities (HASS) Teacher Years 8–12**


Teach HASS Main Lessons and weekly Humanities across Years 8–12 and Year 11 and 12 Elective lessons.

  



**Main Lessons** are extended teaching blocks, taught each morning over several weeks, allowing students and teachers to explore a particular historical period, geographical theme, social issue or area of study in much greater depth. They provide opportunities for rich discussion, research, debate, project work and immersive learning, and are a distinctive and highly valued feature of Steiner education.

  



**Weekly lessons and electives** complement the Main Lessons by providing ongoing development of knowledge and skills in single or double periods.


Our school does not participate in WACE subjects; however, the Steiner curriculum is aligned to the WA Curriculum.

  



**About You**


You are an educator and leader who is organised and brings warmth, clarity, and inspiration. You understand that senior students need both freedom and guidance, and you can hold the rigour of the task, whilst supporting their individual needs, as they take on new levels of responsibility. You bring:


* Experience working with high school students. Preferably Senior students but that is not essential.
* Strong organisational skills and the ability to coordinate multiple projects and people.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills including an above average social emotional intelligence.
* A capacity to mentor both staff and students and a willingness to engage with parents while also being good at keeping your boundaries.
* An openness to working with the principles of Steiner education and supporting the developmental stage of late adolescence.
* Excellent skill, grasp and love of teaching HASS to Years 8 \-12 via a thematic/genre\-based approach.

  



**Essential Requirements:**


* Current TRBWA teacher registration
* Current Working with Children Check
* Right to work in Australia (Please note there is no sponsorship available)

  

**DOE Teachers Welcome**


If you’re currently employed by the Department of Education (DOE), this is your chance to broaden your teaching experience. Consider applying for a one\-year leave without pay to explore this opportunity risk\-free.

  



**How to Apply**


Please send your application, including a covering letter, CV, and the names of two referees, to pscemployment@pws.wa.edu.au


For further information, please email Hayley Spracklen, Head of Campus on hspracklen@pws.wa.edu.au or call the Office on 08 9302 2256\.

**New Graduate Physiotherapist — Caringbah**

Most physios are taught that the job is finished when the pain stops. We think that's roughly where it starts.

Here's the position you'd be signing up to, stated plainly: getting someone out of pain returns them to the exact condition they were in when they got injured. Nothing about their capacity has changed. It's the same body that failed six weeks ago, which is a large part of why they'll be back in six months.

If that reads as obviously true to you, keep going. If it sounds like overservicing, we're genuinely not the clinic for you, and that's fine.

**About Regen Health**

We're an evidence\-based physiotherapy and performance clinic in Caringbah, rated 5\.0 by 70\+ locals. Owner\-operated, and deliberately built as one continuous facility instead of a row of treatment rooms:

* A fully equipped gym with an indoor running track
* Infrared sauna, ice bath and compression boots
* Treatment rooms that open straight onto the gym floor

That layout isn't a perk we tacked on. It's the method. We take people through four stages, and the building is organised around them:

* Assess. Work out what's actually going on, and why.
* Restore. Settle the acute pain, get range of motion back, get them comfortable. Hands\-on lives here.
* Rebuild. Build capacity to well above where they started. Not back to baseline. Past it.
* Regenerate. Hold that capacity and get them properly back into their life.

Most clinics stop somewhere in stage two, because stage two is where the pain goes away and stage three needs equipment they don't have. We're set up so you never have to stop there.

**The role**

A genuinely mentored new\-grad position working directly alongside the clinic owner. You won't be one of twelve. You'll be the second physio in the building, which means the person teaching you is in the next room, not in another suburb.

You'll see the full spread: necks and spines, shoulders, knees, sciatica, tendinopathy, post\-op rehab, workers comp, and the weekend\-warrior damage the Shire reliably produces. Desk workers who've been quietly organising their week around a back that flares. Older adults whose real fear is losing independence. Athletes who want to know how many good years they've got left.

Hands\-on treatment, dry needling, cupping and taping, then load them properly in the gym and take them all the way through.

**What every clinician here is expected to be good at**

This is our actual internal standard, not a wishlist:

* Sound diagnostic ability. Know what you're looking at.
* Genuine hands\-on skills. We use them, we just don't stop there.
* Getting the patient to understand why it matters. If someone doesn't understand the reason for an exercise, they won't do it. That conversation is part of the treatment, not an extra.
* Respecting the flow from physio into strength work. Knowing when hands\-on has done its job and it's time to load.
* A real understanding of exercise, and of what this particular person can currently do, and what they actually want back.

You won't have all five on day one. Nobody does. But that's what we'll instil in you.

**Three things we don't do**

* Passive treatment on its own. No heat packs and electrotherapy.
* Cookie\-cutter exercise with no reasoning behind it.
* Handing over a program without explaining why progression matters.

**What we commit to**

* Weekly 1:1 mentoring. Protected time, every week, with the owner. Real case review, not a corridor chat.
* A deliberately reduced caseload to start. Longer appointments and fewer patients a day for your first few months, so you have room to think.
* In\-house training. Regular hands\-on skills sessions and case\-based teaching.
* Ownership of your own treatment plans. Supported, not supervised into paralysis.

**You'll suit this if**

* You hold AHPRA registration, or will before you start
* You're comfortable in a gym. You can coach a hinge, a squat and a press without googling it
* You're willing to have the harder conversation with someone who wants to stop the moment they feel fine
* You ask questions instead of guessing
* You want to help build something, not just fill a diary

We don't care what your GPA was.

**Hours and pay**

Fully flexible. Full\-time or part\-time, days negotiable.

Clinic hours: Mon\-Thu 8am\-7pm, Fri 8am\-3pm, Sat 8am\-1pm

$75,000\-$90,000 \+ super depending on hours and experience, moving to a percentage of billings once you're ramped, usually around the six\-month mark, so your income grows with your book.

Free run of the gym, sauna and ice bath.

Email your CV to ••••@regenhealth.com.au with a short note answering one question:

Think of a patient you treated on placement who got out of pain. What would you have done with them next, if you'd had another eight weeks and a gym?
